newsitem.title: UK: ISO sees sugar stocks ratio at 36 pct by end 96/97.
newsitem.headline: ISO sees sugar stocks ratio at 36 pct by end 96/97.

text.p: World sugar stocks could reach 43.6 million tonnes by the end of the 1996/97 season and boost the stocks/consumption ratio by two percent to 36 percent, the International Sugar Organization (ISO) said on Thursday. The 36-percent stocks/consumption ratio represented the level traditionally considered to be a strong indicator of an oversupplied market, the ISO said.

In its latest revision to the 1996/97 global sugar balance, based on the October/September crop year, the ISO said it expected stocks to remain at about 41 million tonnes -- the same level as last year.
"But taking into account the excess of export availabilities over import demand, the level of stocks could reach 43.6 million tonnes by the end of the season," it said.

Export availabilities were expected to reach 34.35 million tonnes, a slight upward revision from the ISO's last estimate in September. Global import demand was pegged at 31.65 million tonnes, up from the previous estimate of 30.97 million.
The ISO reiterated its earlier view that the world sugar surplus would continue to weigh on market prices.
"We believe that the overhanging global surplus will keep world market prices under further bearish pressure and the market will enter a period of lower prices," it said.
Prices would be pressured down towards around 10 cents/lb for raw sugar, close to the long-term average, and $280/tonne -- or 12.75 cents/lb -- for standard white sugar, it added.
